card.name: Linking words before newborn-related terms
card.fires_on: Small linking words (in, and, the, a comma) right before the model expects a word about newborns, such as neonates or neonatal. It shows up in pregnancy, delivery and fetal-harm passages.

modes.label: Link before neonatal
modes.description: A linking word or comma after a fetal or pregnancy finding, just before neonatal or neonates.
modes.example: may cause fetal renal dysfunction leading to oligohydramnios and, in some cases<<,>> neonatal renal impairment.

modes.label: Newborn setting in general text
modes.description: A small word in lay text on birth or newborn physiology where a baby-related word comes next.
modes.example: Instead it<< is>> immediately removed from a sterile environment

card.writes: It seems to push toward newborn-related continuations such as neonatal, and away from discharge and premature terms.
card.plain: It fires on small connecting words just before a word about newborns is expected, in pregnancy and delivery text.
